# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-10-04

**Executive summary:** Mainstream visibility is the headline this cycle: **Linus Sebastian** [discussed his **Hermes** setup experience on the latest podcast](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-50bfba4787b6), and the moment was fully organic — **@NousResearch** celebrated the coverage (noting he even pronounced the name right), issued a **[not sponsored](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-24b71d599bb3)** clarification, [reached out to the **Linus Tech Tips** team](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-c3063806d60e) to help them get the most out of Hermes, while **@Teknium** [publicly invited Linus to send suggestions](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-f7e97ee0dd1f) and [teased that something is "coming"](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-0a462830bddf); community sentiment ran so warm that even a simple [hearts reply from Teknium](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-d526aac4d1d0) pulled ~1,005 likes and 30k views. The most substantive original content is roadmap disclosure: [the desktop app is becoming a **web app**](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5fe8d3567c01) usable from anywhere via the **Nous portal** or self-hosted, subscriptions will bundle **hosted Hermes agent instances**, and mobile plans are in development — framed by Nous' [no-model-lock-in philosophy](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-76b17dcaa955) (agent harnesses users can freely modify) as the open-source differentiator. The release picture is unchanged: **[v0.20.0](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49159200)** remains the ship of record with the **v2026.8.3** tag discrepancy still unresolved (verify before pinning version claims), and no releases or merged PRs landed this cycle — the news channel's only candidate was the routine [automated daily sync to hermes-agent-community](/?date=2026-10-04&category=news#item-5df3969bf849) (**5df3969bf849**, 02:00, 2026-10-03), housekeeping already reflected in yesterday's edition. Everything else in the research channel is consolidation of the week's running threads rather than fresh signal: ecosystem tooling matured on three fronts (orchestration via **[verso](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49628094)**'s non-CLI UI layer, observability via **[Grafana](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49318128)** dashboards for long-running agents, memory via **[LanceDB](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49133145)** vector-backed semantic storage), with the **[Refine Cycle](/?date=2026-10-02&category=research#item-hn-49606988)** self-improvement plugin the research channel's top story and the **[Bifrost](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49159529)** router-necessity debate standing in for stack growing pains; multi-agent patterns consolidated around the **[Codex](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49136162)**↔**Claude Code** issue-to-PR skill and first-party **[Hermes Kanban](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49604068)** profile collaboration, with the week's **[Claude Pro/Max subscription support](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49790991)** anchoring the cost-barrier story. Operator-facing risk items persist: the **[hermes-jekyl-hyde](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49231797)** repo documents prompt-injection and adversarial-reversal techniques against hermes-agent, and the [degeneration-loop failure](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49916751) during environment introspection was re-surfaced — caveat: the attribution to **GLM 5.3 Flash** doesn't check out against the model index (the Z.ai line tops out at **GLM-5.2**), so verify what was actually running. Governance friction is now a thread of its own: the standing [~23,000 open-PR backlog](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49424643) on **NousResearch/hermes-agent** (fourth consecutive cycle), a [moderation dispute](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49208206) in which a question was deleted and the user blocked, setup friction candidly documented by commercial adopter **[Almanac](/?date=2026-10-04&category=research#item-hn-49511007)** (YC S26), and an unusually direct Nous acknowledgment on social that the **Discord** team [has not been receptive to stability suggestions](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5a082fb62e61) (raised by **@AdityaTripathiD**) — candor-over-spin that folds into the transparency narrative. On the community side, **rlaope** continued evangelizing [**Oh My Hermes (omh)**](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5ddcc93fdba5) with linked real-world results as adoption evidence. Net read: no new model launches, no Reddit threads, and no user-facing news-channel changes — today's signal is visibility and direction (mainstream spotlight, the web-app/hosted/mobile roadmap, subscription bundling) layered over a consolidation week, with governance friction and unverified model attributions the caveats to watch.
executive_summary_html:
# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-10-04

Executive summary: Mainstream visibility is the headline this cycle: Linus Sebastian discussed his Hermes setup experience on the latest podcast, and the moment was fully organic — @NousResearch celebrated the coverage (noting he even pronounced the name right), issued a not sponsored clarification, reached out to the Linus Tech Tips team to help them get the most out of Hermes, while @Teknium publicly invited Linus to send suggestions and teased that something is "coming"; community sentiment ran so warm that even a simple hearts reply from Teknium pulled ~1,005 likes and 30k views. The most substantive original content is roadmap disclosure: the desktop app is becoming a web app usable from anywhere via the Nous portal or self-hosted, subscriptions will bundle hosted Hermes agent instances, and mobile plans are in development — framed by Nous' no-model-lock-in philosophy (agent harnesses users can freely modify) as the open-source differentiator. The release picture is unchanged: v0.20.0 remains the ship of record with the v2026.8.3 tag discrepancy still unresolved (verify before pinning version claims), and no releases or merged PRs landed this cycle — the news channel's only candidate was the routine automated daily sync to hermes-agent-community (5df3969bf849, 02:00, 2026-10-03), housekeeping already reflected in yesterday's edition. Everything else in the research channel is consolidation of the week's running threads rather than fresh signal: ecosystem tooling matured on three fronts (orchestration via verso's non-CLI UI layer, observability via Grafana dashboards for long-running agents, memory via LanceDB vector-backed semantic storage), with the Refine Cycle self-improvement plugin the research channel's top story and the Bifrost router-necessity debate standing in for stack growing pains; multi-agent patterns consolidated around the Codex↔Claude Code issue-to-PR skill and first-party Hermes Kanban profile collaboration, with the week's Claude Pro/Max subscription support anchoring the cost-barrier story. Operator-facing risk items persist: the hermes-jekyl-hyde repo documents prompt-injection and adversarial-reversal techniques against hermes-agent, and the degeneration-loop failure during environment introspection was re-surfaced — caveat: the attribution to GLM 5.3 Flash doesn't check out against the model index (the Z.ai line tops out at GLM-5.2), so verify what was actually running. Governance friction is now a thread of its own: the standing ~23,000 open-PR backlog on NousResearch/hermes-agent (fourth consecutive cycle), a moderation dispute in which a question was deleted and the user blocked, setup friction candidly documented by commercial adopter Almanac (YC S26), and an unusually direct Nous acknowledgment on social that the Discord team has not been receptive to stability suggestions (raised by @AdityaTripathiD) — candor-over-spin that folds into the transparency narrative. On the community side, rlaope continued evangelizing Oh My Hermes (omh) with linked real-world results as adoption evidence. Net read: no new model launches, no Reddit threads, and no user-facing news-channel changes — today's signal is visibility and direction (mainstream spotlight, the web-app/hosted/mobile roadmap, subscription bundling) layered over a consolidation week, with governance friction and unverified model attributions the caveats to watch.

top_items.title: Belkin killed my smart switch. I got it working again without their app
top_items.content:
I bought a wifi switch from Belkin over 10 years ago, but the app got turned off.

I wanted to use the switch to automate my mosquito repellent. Unfortunately it still had my timer running from Christmas, which meant it turned off too early. It ruined my last night's sleep.

First thing in the morning I opened the app and wanted to change the timer.

The app was offline and I read online that it is discontinued. The switch is basically garbage now.

I was pissed at first, but then I gav

social.category_summary:
**Headline — Mainstream spotlight:** The batch is dominated by **Linus Sebastian** [discussing his **Hermes** setup experience on the latest podcast](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-50bfba4787b6). **@NousResearch** [publicly celebrated the organic coverage](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-50bfba4787b6) (noting he even pronounced the name right), [reached out to the **Linus Tech Tips** team to help them get the most out of Hermes](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-c3063806d60e), and issued a [**not sponsored** clarification](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-24b71d599bb3) — underscoring that the buzz was fully organic. **@Teknium** [openly invited Linus to send suggestions](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-f7e97ee0dd1f) and [teased that something is "coming"](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-0a462830bddf) in the thread. Community sentiment is celebratory; even [Teknium's simple hearts reply](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-d526aac4d1d0) pulled ~1,005 likes and 30k views, mirroring the mood around the mention.

**Product roadmap:** The most substantive original content is [Teknium's disclosure that the desktop app is becoming a **web app**](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5fe8d3567c01) usable from anywhere via the **Nous portal** or self-hosted, that subscriptions will bundle **hosted Hermes agent instances**, with mobile plans also in the works. Alongside it, Nous articulated a core philosophy: use agent harnesses with [**no model lock-in**](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-76b17dcaa955) that users can freely modify — a differentiator message that resonates strongly with the open-source community.

**Transparency on friction:** Nous candidly acknowledged that the [**Discord** team has not been receptive to suggestions](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5a082fb62e61) for more stable agent setup — an honest acknowledgment of third-party platform pain raised by community members like **@AdityaTripathiD**; notable for its candor rather than spin.

**Community projects:** **rlaope** is actively evangelizing **Oh My Hermes (omh)**, [sharing linked real-world results as evidence for why people should adopt](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5ddcc93fdba5) the community-built tooling.

**Low-content tail:** A long tail of emoji-only acknowledgments (hearts, fire, eyes, salutes) from **@Teknium** and **@NousResearch** toward the [**Thursdai podcast** crew](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-5bb77cb278e3), [@HermesAgentTips](/?date=2026-10-04&category=social#item-d639cecd05af), and other community figures — social glue with little newsletter value, excluded from the top ranks.

@Mattmaximo @didier_lopes I think you're missing two other things. 

1. We are making the desktop app a web app, so you can use it like perplexity computer, just sign into nous portal and use the app, or run it yourself like the dashboard and access it from anything and anywhere.

2. A Hermes instance with every sub. No added cost, no complexity to setting up a server. Just sign up and you have a ready to go agent with a meaningfully useful computer, and sign up from anywhere, imsg, the future mobile app, the web, telegram, slack, you name it

On your first three, #3 is done internally, rolling out soon.

#2 is coming. We have 3 people with great experience or work on mobile apps onboarding and it's coming

#1 I'll let @imbabybrooklyn take
